data.title: Deployment
data.tagline: Build the project and make it available on a server
data.description: Deployment turns source code into a running website or service. It may install dependencies, build assets, set environment variables, start processes, and connect a domain. A repeatable deployment includes logs, health checks, and a way to return to a known working version.

avoid: Deploy unreviewed secrets or local-only settings
Assume a successful build means the service is healthy
Change production manually with no record
Release without knowing how to roll back

lessonPractice.title: Code is merged. How do you confirm users are actually receiving the new version?

options.label: Confirm build and deployment success, then check a version signal and key path on production
options.feedback: Correct. Merge is not release; verify both the platform and the real user entry point.

options.label: Announce release when main has the new commit
options.feedback: Build, deployment, cache, or environment configuration can still leave production on an old version.

options.label: Count a working local page as production updated
options.feedback: Local behavior cannot prove the production build and release.

data.agentPrompt: Deploy the current commit to the authorized test environment without touching production. Record the commit hash, target project, and environment. After successful build and deployment logs, open the test URL and verify its version signal plus the sign-in entry. Stop on any failure and report the stage and log evidence.
